items.followUp: Write four properties of cathode rays.

rubric.why: Identifies the positive charge of the particles in canal rays.
rubric.description: Canal rays consist of positively charged particles (positive ions).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that canal rays carry a positive charge or consist of positive ions.

rubric.description: Canal rays travel in straight lines.

rubric.why: States their deflection direction in an electric field.
rubric.description: They are deflected towards the negative plate, opposite to cathode rays.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that they deflect towards the negative plate or opposite to cathode rays.

accept: depends on the nature of the gas
rubric.why: Identifies that canal-ray properties vary with the gas used.
rubric.description: Their properties, including their charge-to-mass ratio, depend on the nature of the gas in the discharge tube.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that their properties or charge-to-mass ratio depend on the gas in the tube.

modelAnswer: Canal rays consist of positively charged particles (positive ions).
They are deflected towards the negative plate and in a direction opposite to cathode rays.
Their properties, including their charge-to-mass ratio, depend on the nature of the gas in the discharge tube.

items.followUp: Write five physical properties of non-metals.

rubric.why: Identifies the lustrous appearance of metals.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that metals are lustrous or shiny.

rubric.why: Identifies that metals can be beaten into sheets.
rubric.description: Metals are malleable and can be beaten into thin sheets.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that metals are malleable.

rubric.why: Identifies that metals can be drawn into wires.
rubric.description: Metals are ductile and can be drawn into wires.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that metals are ductile.

rubric.description: Metals are good conductors of electricity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that metals conduct electricity well.

rubric.description: Metals are good conductors of heat.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that metals conduct heat well.

modelAnswer: Metals are generally lustrous, or shiny.
Metals are malleable and can be beaten into thin sheets.
Metals are ductile and can be drawn into wires.
Metals are good conductors of electricity.
Metals are good conductors of heat.

items.followUp: Calculate the molecular mass of carbon dioxide, CO₂. (C = 12 u, O = 16 u)

rubric.why: Uses the correct atomic masses and atom counts for water.
rubric.description: Molecular mass of H₂O = 2(1 u) + 16 u.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct calculation using two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.

rubric.why: Gives the correct molecular mass with an appropriate unit.
rubric.description: Molecular mass of H₂O = 18 u (18 amu).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct final value with an appropriate unit.

modelAnswer: Given: H = 1 u and O = 16 u.

items.followUp: Define a formula unit and give the formula unit of magnesium chloride.

rubric.why: Defines a formula unit as the simplest ratio of ions in an ionic compound.
rubric.description: A formula unit is the simplest whole-number ratio of ions in an ionic compound.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this definition or an equivalent statement.

rubric.why: Provides a valid example and its formula unit.
rubric.description: For example, NaCl is the formula unit of sodium chloride.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct example.

modelAnswer: A formula unit is the simplest whole-number ratio of ions in an ionic compound.
For example, NaCl is the formula unit of sodium chloride.

items.followUp: State the general trend of atomic radius across a period and down a group.

rubric.why: Gives the general period trend in electron affinity.
rubric.description: Electron affinity generally increases from left to right across a period.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that electron affinity increases across a period.

rubric.why: Gives the general group trend in electron affinity.
rubric.description: Electron affinity generally decreases down a group.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that electron affinity decreases down a group.

modelAnswer: Across a period, electron affinity generally increases from left to right.
Down a group, electron affinity generally decreases.
